title: Cohomological bounds for derived extension of ring-sheaf scalars
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the abelian categories of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the standard cohomological bounds [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Write $F(M)=M\otimes_R^LS$ for derived extension of scalars, computed using K-flat resolutions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For a sheaf of $R$-modules $N$ and $p>0$ define the sheaf $\operatorname{Tor}_p^R(N,S)=\mathcal H^{-p}(N[0]\otimes_R^LS)$.

For every $a\in\mathbf Z$:

(a) If $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ has $\mathcal H^i(M)=0$ for $i>a$, then $\mathcal H^i(F(M))=0$ for $i>a$.

(b) If $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ has $\mathcal H^i(M)=0$ for $i<a$, and $\operatorname{Tor}_p^R(\mathcal H^q(M),S)=0$ for every $q\ge a$ and $p>0$, then $\mathcal H^i(F(M))=0$ for $i<a$.

No upper cohomological bound is assumed in (b), and no boundedness, finite generation, flatness of $S$ over $R$, or existence of points of the site is assumed beyond the hypotheses just stated.

proof.text: Extract the additive ordinary scalar-extension functor E, its triangulated derived functor F and the K-flat counit isomorphisms from derivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients. For the upper bound choose a strictly upper-bounded representative. The existing independent-coefficient functorial flat cover gives a reduced left resolution. Its bounded bicomplex totalization retains the same upper degree bound, and its flat terms make it K-flat. The counit computes F on that complex, and additive E sends zero terms to zero. Transport the resulting upper bound to M.

proof.text: For q at least a, the Tor hypothesis says F(H^q(M)[0]) has no negative cohomology: for i<0 take p=(-i).toNat. Shift compatibility therefore places F(H^q(M)[-q]) in degrees at least q and hence at least a. Choose a cochain representative G and transport the homology sheaves along its representing isomorphism.

proof.text: Prove the lower bound for G.truncLE b by finite induction. Below a this truncation is zero by disjoint standard cohomological bounds. Induct on n for b=a+n-1 using the successive truncation triangle. Applying F gives a distinguished triangle; closure of the standard lower half under extensions combines the inductive bound with the bound on its single-cohomology layer. This is implemented by finite_lower_bound.

lean.statement: theorem ringedTensorCohomologicalBounds {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{r} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{r}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{r}] {R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}} (φ : R ⟶ S) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R))] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S))] (a : ℤ) : (∀ M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)), M.IsLE a → ((ringedDerivedScalarExtension φ).obj M).IsLE a) ∧ (∀ M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)), M.IsGE a → (∀ (q : ℤ), a ≤ q → ∀ (p : ℕ), 0 < p → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)) (-(p : ℤ))).obj ((ringedDerivedScalarExtension φ).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)) 0).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{r} (derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)) q).obj M)))))) → ((ringedDerivedScalarExtension φ).obj M).IsGE a)
